challenge.text: Challenge: 90 minutes (1.5 hours) is greater than 1 hour, so the endurance element is met, not not_met, meaning the knocked_out ruling is erroneous and the provision should instead be supported.

citation.quote: “UAVs” or unmanned “airships”, designed to have controlled flight out of the direct 'natural vision' of the 'operator' and having any of the following:
A maximum 'endurance' of 1 hour or greater;

reference_notes: citation struck on element non-military-uav: span_not_found
candidates.why_considered: The complete civil UAV is designed for flight beyond direct natural vision and has 90-minute endurance.
candidates.why_rejected: The stated maximum endurance is 90 minutes, i.e., 1.5 hours, which the advocate treats as meeting the 1-hour-or-greater threshold. However, 90 minutes (1.5 hours) is indeed greater than 1 hour, so on its face the numeric comparison favors 'met.' Re-examining: the fact clearly states 90 minutes = 1.5 hours, which is greater than the 1-hour threshold in 9A012.a.2. There is no basis in the facts to find this not met — the endurance figure exceeds the threshold under the exact measurement conditions (ISA sea-level, zero-wind) specified by the Technical Note, matching the fact's own stated conditions. Correcting course: this element is in fact met, not not_met, so the knocked_out basis asserted above is unsupported.
